correctness.rationale: Any scalar-linear extension is given at the new point by real weights summing to one. The exact equilateral Kantorovich–Rubinstein norm of delta_i-sum w_j delta_j is phi_i=(|1-w_i|+sum_{j≠i}|w_j|)/2, so ||E||=max(1,max_i phi_i/r_i). If w has negative coefficients with total negative mass t, the renormalized nonnegative vector w_i^+/(1+t) strictly decreases every phi_i; hence the new-point minimax is attained only nonnegatively. For probability weights phi_i=1-w_i. The feasibility function F(z)=sum_i(1-z r_i)_+ is strictly decreasing through one and the sorted-prefix constraints give z=max_{k>=2}(k-1)/sum_{i<=k}r_(i). At root F(z)=1, lower bounds saturate uniquely; z>=1 thereby gives one global optimal weight even at equality z=1. For z<1 strict optimality slack creates a relative open neighborhood in the coefficient-sum hyperplane; the full optimal polytope is exactly phi_i<=r_i for all i and is bounded. A negative entry w_j<0 forces r_j>1, while r_j>1 permits perturbation from a strictly feasible zero-j weight to negative after distributing F(1)<1 slack. Independently checked rational examples 4/3,1,5/6 and valid signed witness; finite LP/checker is corroboration only.

final_claim: For arbitrary admissible radii of a point added to an n-point equilateral metric, the sharp real scalar-linear extension norm is max(1,z), z=max_{2<=k<=n}(k-1)/sum_{i<=k}r_(i); among all signed coefficient vectors, the new-point minimax barycenter is unique w_i=(1-z r_i)_+. The complete optimal-coefficient equality set is a singleton for z>=1 and a full-dimensional signed polytope for z<1; negative optimal coefficients occur exactly when z<1 and some radius exceeds one.
